title: Forging legal contracts and smart contracts using the Minimum Hybrid Contract (MHC)
authors: Jørgen Svennevik Notland, Jakob Svennevik Notland, Donn Morrison
description: Conference presentation of the MHC paper.

title: The Minimum Hybrid Contract (MHC): Combining Legal and Blockchain Smart Contracts
meta: EASE 2020, 24th International Conference on Evaluation and Assessment in Software Engineering, ACM
authors: Jørgen Svennevik Notland, Jakob Svennevik Notland, Donn Morrison
description: Proposes the Minimum Hybrid Contract: an online smart contract immutably linked to an offline legal contract, so that a contract's financial transactions become auditable, transparent and immutable while disputes stay with the civil courts. Preprint on arXiv, February 2020.

title: The Minimum Hybrid Contract (MHC): Combining Legal and Blockchain Smart Contracts
meta: NTNU School of Entrepreneurship, Norwegian University of Science and Technology
authors: Jørgen Svennevik Notland. Supervisors: Roger Sørheim and Donn Morrison
description: Having identified contracts as the nexus of corruption, the thesis asks how contracts, blockchain smart contracts and financial regulation can be combined to make contracts secure, accountable, transparent and inclusive, and introduces the term Minimum Hybrid Contract.

title: Blockchain enabled Trust & Transparency in supply chains
meta: NTNU School of Entrepreneurship, Norwegian University of Science and Technology
authors: Jørgen Svennevik Notland, Anders Viet Hua
description: Investigates the nature of trust in supply chains and whether blockchain can increase it. Blockchain gives high integrity but unstable information reliability: how data is recorded on-chain is the critical step, and actors need a clear incentive before they adopt it.
note: Google Scholar lists this thesis under two records (12 and 5 citations); 17 is the sum. Counts overlap between sources, so they are not added together.
